pr.title: Keep the store unlocked behind Touch ID between commands
pr.head: 0f393177e19fb206dd062ea7d64475986a13495b

summary: Today every multipass command asks for the passphrase, so looking up a username, a password, and a one-time code means typing it three times. This pull request keeps the store unlocked between commands without giving up what the prompt guarantees: a program running as you, an AI coding agent included, still cannot read or change an entry without a person at the Mac.

It works like this. After a command asks for the passphrase and succeeds, it starts a background agent, multipass __agent, as its own child process, and hands it the vault key over the child's stdin. The vault key is the random key that encrypts the store's files, and the passphrase encrypts the vault key, so the agent never needs the passphrase. Later commands ask the agent over a Unix socket instead of prompting. The agent shows a Touch ID or Apple Watch sheet that names the entry, such as "multipass is trying to read github.com", and answers only once a person approves that one request.

1. One entry per request. read, list, and edit each need their own approval. A reply holds only the named entry, and a save that touches any other entry is refused.
  2. A decline ends the session. Cancelling a sheet, or leaving it for 60 seconds, replies denied and ends the agent. When no one can approve, as with the lid closed, the agent replies unavailable and the command asks for the passphrase.
  3. Sessions end on their own. The agent ends when the vault key reaches its deadline, 21 days after the key was made, on multipass lock, when another Mac rotates the key, and when the multipass executable changes on disk. It writes an end note beside its socket, so the next prompt can say why it asks again, such as Passphrase (you declined a request): .

init, passwd, and rekey always prompt, and passwd and rekey replace the agent. MULTIPASS_NO_AGENT=1 and an SSH login, which sets SSH_CONNECTION, keep the prompt on every command. Off macOS the code compiles, but no agent starts.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Agent: the background multipass __agent process that holds the vault key between commands.
  • Vault key: the random key that encrypts the store files. The passphrase encrypts it in the key file.
  • Sheet: the macOS Touch ID or Apple Watch approval dialog.
  • Start message: the deadline and the key file's text, written once to the agent's stdin.
  • End note: <hash>.ended, beside the socket, saying why the last agent ended.
  • Stale: the agent's key no longer opens the store, because a rotation ran elsewhere.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One review, across three heads, requested changes with six open findings, all flagged on the lines below.
  • A push during the review fixed prompts that said the session ended while the agent still served.
  • The Touch ID sheet itself was not exercised. The owner checks the plan's sheet rows by hand.
  • The plan file stays a draft at this head, until the Touch ID prototype's plan edit merges.

groups.title: The agent and its protocol
groups.kicker: What the agent holds, who may talk to it, and what each message does
intro: src/agent.rs holds both halves of the session agent. The agent half reads the start message from stdin, binds ~/.multipass/agent/<hash>.sock, where the hash names the store, and answers each connection on its own thread. The client half is what every other command uses to connect, check the agent, and send one request.

Every request is one line of ASCII, followed by a counted run of bytes where it carries a name or store text. read, list, and edit go through the Approver trait, which Touch ID implements and the tests replace with a fake, one sheet at a time. status and lock need no approval: the first reveals only that an agent runs, and the second can only end it.

The other end runs as yougetpeereid, on both sides
The agent runs the same executable file as the clientconnect, from LOCAL_PEERPID and proc_pidpath, comparing device, inode, size, and change time
The agent's own executable has not changedunfit, before every approval

checks.text: The vault key never crosses the socket. A process running as you could bind the socket path while no agent runs, so the key goes only down the stdin pipe of a child the command started itself.

files.note: The whole agent: the start message, the socket and its checks, the request handlers, the end note, and the client.

checks.text: cargo test passes at this head (133 and 1 tests). The agent tests run a real agent on a socket in /tmp with a fake approver, so no sheet appears.

The start message is read through io::stdin(), whose 8 KiB buffer keeps a copy of the keys for the agent's whole life. That copy is neither pinned out of swap nor wiped, so the README's "locked out of swap" promises more than the agent does.

end sets ended before it writes the note and before the handler writes its reply, and serve exits as soon as its 50 ms poll sees the flag. The process can then exit first, so lock prints Not unlocked, or a decline fails with a protocol error.
This test's docstring tells the bug's history rather than stating the rule the test checks.

groups.title: Opening the store with the keys alone
groups.kicker: How the agent reads and saves the package without the passphrase
intro: A prompted command opens the package with the passphrase. The agent has only the key file's text, which Session::agent_keys gives it: the current vault key and the keys it replaced in the last 90 days. Vault::open_with_keys opens the package from those keys, and fails with Error::Stale when the package holds a key file or a store file of a generation the keys do not cover.

A session opened this way is unlocked. It may save store files, but it never rotates the key or writes a key file, because only the passphrase can encrypt one. Session::session_deadline is the key's creation time plus 21 days, so every Mac's session for one key ends at the same moment. src/store.rs gains Store::only for one-entry replies, and Store::all_names for the check that a save names only the edited entry.

files.note: The keys-only open, the agent's key text and deadline, and a shared helper that decrypts the store files.

checks.text: writable now passes for an unlocked session, and rotate still refuses one, because it has no passphrase. An agent starts only from a prompted session that is writable, so a read-only package never gets one.
The agent's open skips the package's move records, so reads through the agent never see what another Mac on an older multipass saved to the old single-file store, until a prompt merges it.

The session-unlock plan stays status: draft, and its § 2.11 still says this file and src/store.rs gain no code. The rule in AGENTS.md asks for the plan to change in the change that settles its decisions.

files.note: only and all_names, and escape and unescape made public for the sheet's text and the names list.

groups.title: Touch ID and the system calls
groups.kicker: The unsafe modules behind the agent's approval and hardening
intro: These modules hold the new unsafe code, each behind a safe interface, as AGENTS.md requires. src/touch_id.rs loads LocalAuthentication with dlopen only in an agent, and asks with policy 4, a finger on Touch ID or a press on a paired watch, never the login password. Each request gets a fresh LAContext. unavailable comes only from canEvaluatePolicy before a sheet shows. Once a sheet shows, anything but a touch is denied, so a cancel never falls back to the passphrase.

LocalAuthentication answers in an Objective-C block, a callback object, on a queue of its own. src/objc.rs builds a global block by hand, with no captured state, and the block hands the result to the waiting agent thread through a channel. src/sys.rs wraps the libSystem calls: the peer's user and process, setsid so closing the terminal does not end the agent, PT_DENY_ATTACH against debuggers, no core files, mlock, and a wipe that the compiler cannot remove.

checks.text: A probe program of the reviewer's own showed that, after a rename over a running executable's path, proc_pidpath still reports that path, so an upgrade in place passes the client's check and the old agent then detects the change itself.

files.note: The approval itself: availability first, then one sheet, a 60-second wait, and invalidate.
The global block that carries evaluatePolicy's reply, and reading an NSError's code.
Safe wrappers for the peer checks and the agent's memory hardening, with fallbacks off macOS.
Off macOS: nothing can approve, so no agent starts.

groups.title: The commands that use the agent
groups.kicker: Which commands ask the agent, and when they prompt instead
intro: src/main.rs routes each command through a Ctx, which tries the agent first and prompts when it must. get, history, list, and otp read through the agent. add, rm, restore, otp --set, and otp --clear change one entry through an edit and a save. Each falls back to the passphrase on unavailable, stale, or no agent, and fails on denied.

A command that prompted starts a fresh agent once it succeeds. status prints unlocked until … or locked and the end note's reason. lock ends the session. The prompt's reason comes from what the command found when it tried the agent, recorded as Tried.

checks.text: Driving the release build with expect under a temporary HOME, MULTIPASS_NO_AGENT=1 and SSH_CONNECTION each kept the prompt and started no agent. status and lock reported no session, and an agent directory at mode 0755 was named and refused.

files.note: The agent-first open for each command, status and lock, and replacing the agent after passwd and rekey.

checks.text: lock and status treat an agent that runs from another multipass executable file as no agent. So a second install prints Not unlocked while the first install's agent still holds the key.

groups.title: Documentation and rules
groups.kicker: What the README, AGENTS.md, and the passkeys plan now say
intro: The README gains a section, "Stay unlocked between commands", on the touch for each request, when a session ends, status, lock, and what the agent exposes. It drops "Session unlock" from the list of work not built yet. AGENTS.md names the four modules that may hold unsafe code, and adds the rule that the agent gives the vault key to no one. The passkeys plan's sentence about the CLI now points at session unlock.
